claims: Anthropic API key is gone entirely; runs through Claude Max subscription
Faster responses, real persistent memory (markdown files), can brainstorm a build before launching Claude in the background
Can send messages into existing Claude Code sessions, not just ones it started
Dashboard tabs: Runs, Sessions (incl. which are waiting on you), Projects, Specs (review/approve planned builds), Memory, Usage (5-hour and weekly limits)
how_to_steps: Follow the README setup (uses a Claude Max login rather than an API key)
Talk to Jarvis to plan a build, approve the spec in the dashboard, let it run Claude Code in the background
Edit memory markdown files directly if needed; watch usage tab against subscription limits
on_screen_only: Animated green particle-sphere 'Jarvis' visualizer on top monitor

Dashboard with tabs RUNS / SPECS / PROJECTS / USAGE, usage bars '22% 7-DAY WEEK resets Sep 11 4:00am', counters '3028 CONVERSATIONS', '241 PROJECTS', '2.4B CACHE READ', '2.4B CACHE WRITTEN', note 'there is no separate per-model window -- no Fable limit...'
ORCHA terminal/log pane on second monitor

relevance.why: Very close to the founder's own setup: a Claude-Code-orchestrating assistant with memory, specs approval and usage tracking on a Max plan. The 'specs approve then background build' and usage dashboard patterns are directly reusable.

implement_score.why: Worth cloning to study the Claude Code session orchestration and usage-tracking code, then lifting ideas (spec approval gate, memory as markdown, usage meter) rather than adopting a hobby voice stack wholesale. Check that driving Claude Code via a Max login is within Anthropic terms.

verify: Does github.com/ethanplusai/jarvis exist, and how is it licensed/maintained?
How it authenticates through Claude Max (OAuth of the CLI?) and whether that complies with Anthropic's consumer terms
Does it depend on macOS-only voice pieces?
What 'Orcha' is -- part of the repo or a separate tool
